hook: A U.S. military Mission Report documenting two separate UAP sightings within a single operational period, one involving a lone object at constant low speed and a second involving two objects that accelerated and changed direction.
why_it_matters: This MISREP captures two distinct UAP events with specific grid coordinates, altitudes, and velocities, providing the kind of structured, quantitative military reporting that forms the evidentiary backbone of AARO's case database. The second event's combination of speed estimation (278 knots) and apparent maneuvering (acceleration and southward direction change) puts it in the category of objects exhibiting non-passive flight behavior as observed by a military operator. The heavy 1.4(a) redactions across four of six pages mean the operator identity, platform, and broader tactical context remain classified, limiting independent analysis.

key_findings.finding: A single UAP was observed at 1354Z traveling at 40 knots between FL160 and FL170 with constant velocity, with a precise MGRS grid coordinate recorded.

quotes.text: AT 1354Z, 1.4(a)OBSERVED 1X UAP IVO 34SCE7566990098. VELOCITY WAS 40 KNOTS AT FL160 TO FL170. UAP SPEED REMAINED CONSTANT.

key_findings.finding: A second event, nearly nine hours later, involved two possible UAPs estimated at 278 knots that actively accelerated and changed direction to the south.

quotes.text: AT 2243Z, 1.4(a) OBSERVED 2X POSS UAPS IVO 35TQK1580995087. VELOCITY WAS ESTIMATED AT 278 KNOTS. UAPS INCREASED SPEED AND CHANGED DIRECTION TOWARDS THE SOUTH.

key_findings.finding: Both GENTEXT entries are classified SECRET/RELEASABLE (S//REL), indicating the observations were deemed sensitive enough for a classified report but cleared for release to allied partners.
Four of six pages are entirely redacted under the 1.4(a) national security exemption, withholding the operator identity, platform type, and all contextual mission information.

The two sightings differ markedly in speed — 40 knots vs. an estimated 278 knots — suggesting either two distinct object types or the same object class operating at very different regimes across the two events.

quotes.text: VELOCITY WAS 40 KNOTS AT FL160 TO FL170. UAP SPEED REMAINED CONSTANT.
VELOCITY WAS ESTIMATED AT 278 KNOTS. UAPS INCREASED SPEED AND CHANGED DIRECTION TOWARDS THE SOUTH.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The official description explicitly states U.S. military services use MISREPs to report UAP to AARO, making this document a direct AARO intake record.
The S//REL classification marks the report as releasable to allied intelligence partners, indicating the observations were shared within a coalition intelligence framework.
